chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad, from al-Sulami, from Dawud al-Raqqi, who said:

Some of the Khawarij asked me about this verse: 'Of sheep, two; and of goats, two. Say: Has He forbidden the two males or the two females? Or what is in the wombs of the two females? Tell me with knowledge, if you are truthful. And of camels, two; and of cows, two.' What is that which Allah has permitted from that, and what is that which He has prohibited? But I did not have anything (to answer with).

So I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) while I was a pilgrim, and I informed him of what had happened. He said: 'Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, permitted in the sacrificial offering in Mina the domestic sheep and the domestic goat, and prohibited that one sacrifice the mountain (wild) ones.'

And as for His words 'And of camels, two; and of cows, two', indeed Allah, Blessed and High, permitted in the sacrificial offering the Iraab camel, and prohibited the Bukhaty in it; and permitted the domestic cow that one sacrifice with it, and prohibited the mountain (wild) one.
So I returned to the man and informed him with this answer. He said: 'This is something which the camels carried from Al-Hijaaz.'
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between domestic and wild animals for Hajj sacrifices according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the Quranic verse 6:143-143 refers to the specific characteristics of sacrificial animals in Mina, distinguishing between domesticated ('Ahlīyah') and wild/mountainous ('Jabaliyah') varieties of sheep, goats, camels, and cattle. This narration highlights the Shia scholarly approach to interpreting general Quranic verses through specific Prophetic traditions, resolving the ambiguity of 'which two?' by linking it to the practical requirements of the Udhiyah sacrifice. The context underscores the importance of animal suitability for ritual sacrifice, a key topic in Fiqh al-Udhiyah.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibrahim Bin Muhammad, from Al Sulamy, from Dawood Al Raqqy who said,

‘One of the Khawarijites asked me about these Verses [6:143] two of sheep and two of goats. Say: Has He forbidden the two males or the two females [6:144] And two of camels and two of cows – what is that which Allahazwj has Permitted from that, and what is that which Heazwj has Prohibited?’ But, I did not have anything with me (to answer him with)’.

So I went over to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, and I was a pilgrim for Hajj. So I informed him<sup>asws</sup> with what (the matter) was, and he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Permitted regarding the sacrificial offering in Mina, the sheep, and the domesticated goat, and Prohibited that you sacrifice the mountain (goats).

And as for Hisazwj Words [6:144] And two of camels and two of cows, so Allahazwj Blessed and High Permitted regarding the sacrificial offering, the Iraab camel, and Prohibited the Bukhaty; and Permitted the domesticated cow that you offer a sacrifice with it, and Prohibited the wild ones’.

So I left to go to the man, and informed him with this answer. So he said, ‘This is something which the camels carried from Al-Hijaaz (meaning - this is not your answer, but it comes from Al-Hijaaz)’.
en.sarwar: 17. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad from al-Sullamiy from Dawud al-Riqqiy who has said the following: “

Certain persons of al-Khawarij asked me about this verse of al-Quran: ‘Of two sheep and of two goats, ask which one is made unlawful? (Is it) male or female? [6:142] (What is the meaning of) camels two and of cows two?’ [6:143] ‘What Allah has made lawful and what has He made unlawful?’ I did not have any answer.

I went to see abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, when I was there for al- Hajj. I informed him (the Imam) of the story and he (the Imam) said, ‘Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, for sacrifice in Mina’, has made domesticated sheep and goats lawful. He has made the wild ones unlawful,

and His words, ‘Of camels two and of cows two’, means that Allah, most Blessed, most High, has made al-Trab camels lawful for offering as sacrifice and has made unlawful what is al- Bukhatiy. He has made domesticated cows lawful for offering as sacrifice and the wild ones unlawful.’
I returned to the man and informed him of the answer. He said, ‘This is something which camel has carried on its back from al-Hijaz.’”
